title: More Japanese Seniors Are Starting Businesses
paragraphs: In Japan, many people retire in their 60s. But a growing number of older people are choosing to start their own businesses instead.

According to research by Teikoku Databank, a Japanese research company, 20.5% of new companies started in 2025 were led by people aged 60 or older. That was 3.2 percentage points higher than the year before, and it was the first time the number had gone above 20%.

In total, about 156,000 new companies were started in Japan in 2025, which was a record. People in their 40s were still the largest group of business founders, but the number of retired people starting businesses is growing.

There are several reasons for this trend. Japan's population is getting older quickly, and many seniors want to keep working and stay active. Older people also have a lot of experience and large personal networks, which can help them build a successful business.

Starting a business has also become easier for seniors, thanks to more support from the government. For example, they can get free advice from experts, attend networking events and receive financial help. In Tokyo, a support center for small businesses is holding a competition where people aged 55 and over can present their business plans. In Nara Prefecture, people can get up to 2 million yen to help them start a business.

Mio Katagiri, the president of Ginza Second Life, a company that helps seniors start businesses, said there are fewer hurdles than before, thanks to stronger government support. Katagiri also said that, unlike young people, seniors are encouraged to start businesses that they can realistically manage.
Chizuko Fukatsu, who started a clothing company in her 60s, said the strength of seniors is the experience they can use when starting a business.
